title: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head P (Ministry of Home Affairs)

sections.label: Terrorism financing and arrests
sections.summary: Two Singaporeans were charged with terrorism financing, and 723 arrests were made in 2018, mostly involving dangerous weapons and drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Last year, two Singaporeans were charged with terrorism financing, transmitting money to fund terrorist causes overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In 2018 alone, they made 723 arrests, with most offenders possessing dangerous weapons and drugs.

sections.label: Home Team COVID-19 deployment
sections.summary: Maplecroft estimated civil unrest in nearly 40% of countries in 2020, and the MP asked about Home Team deployment against COVID-19 and a future outbreak SOP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: In fact, Maplecroft, a company that specialises in global risk data and country risk analysis, estimated that nearly 40% of the world’s 195 countries will see civil unrest during 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Over and above its everyday duties to keep law and order in Singapore, the Home Team has stepped up to the plate to ensure many quarantine centres are manned and protected and contact tracing carried out effectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: My question is: would the Minister provide an update on the deployment of our Home Team officers towards the national fight against COVID-19 and whether we can build a precedent or a standard operating procedure (SOP) arising from current operational experiences that officers can refer to in a future outbreak?

sections.label: Singapore safety rankings
sections.summary: A Gallup poll found 94% felt safe walking at night, and Singapore ranked first in the Global Order Index and Order and Security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In the latest Gallup poll, 94% of the residents or Singaporeans felt very safe to walk around the neighbourhood at night, and we were ranked first in the whole Global Order Index.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We were also ranked first in Order and Security in the world.

sections.label: Incidents and supermarket crowds
sections.summary: Such incidents destabilise communities, cause social rifts and hurt the economy, and Police managed supermarket crowds after DORSCON Orange.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Such incidents not only destabilise communities, they also cause social rifts and hurt the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I understand that recently, the Police had to be called in to help manage the crowds in at least one of the supermarkets after the Disease Outbreak Response System Condition (DORSCON) was raised to Orange.

sections.label: Citizen births and marriages
sections.summary: Between 2009 and 2015 about 15,000 citizen children were born to non-resident foreign mothers, and in 2018 one in four citizen marriages involved a non-resident.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Between 2009 and 2015, around 15,000 citizen children were born to non-resident foreign mothers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2018, one in four citizen marriages involved a non-resident.

sections.label: HTX technology roadmap focus
sections.summary: The MP asked what areas of focus are in HTX's technology roadmap for border security and critical infrastructure protection research and procurement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, with the formation of HTX with responsibility in research and procurement areas of border security and protection of critical infrastructures, what are the areas of focus in its technology roadmap?

sections.label: HTX talent strategy
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to share more on HTX's talent strategy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Could the Minister share more on HTX’s talent strategy?

sections.label: PolCam deployment and effectiveness
sections.summary: The passage asks for an update on PolCam deployment and effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Can I ask for an update on PolCam deployment and effectiveness?

sections.label: York study on loot boxes
sections.summary: A separate study by academics in York gives some evidence linking loot boxes to problem gambling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: From a separate study by academics in York, there is some evidence linking loot boxes to problem gambling.

sections.label: Regulating youths' loot box access
sections.summary: Singapore ought to consider regulations limiting youths' access to micro-transaction-driven loot boxes to prevent habituation to gambling-like behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Singapore ought to consider implementing, at the very least, regulations to limit access to micro-transaction-driven loot boxes by youths, so as to prevent habituation to addictive gambling-like behaviour among young gamers.

sections.label: Extending officers' retirement and re-employment
sections.summary: The passage asks whether officers' retirement age can be extended from 55 to 62 and re-employment to 65, with early retirement and an Employment Assistance Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Can we extend the retirement age of our officers from 55 to 62, and re-employment to 65?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Optional early retirement could still be offered at age 55, if they prefer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Officers should also be offered an Employment Assistance Package if they are found unsuitable for re-employment.

sections.label: New drug abusers arrested 2019
sections.summary: New drug abusers arrested in 2019 rose 8% from 2018, and about 61% of the 1,469 arrested were below 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The total number of new drug abusers arrested in 2019 increased by 8% from 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Of the 1,469 new drug abusers who were arrested in 2019, about 61% were below 30 years old.

sections.label: New drug users under 35
sections.summary: Last year the highest number of new drug users were aged under 35, and MHA said CNB develops social media content on Singapore's drug policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Indeed, last year, the highest number of new drug users were those aged under 35.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, MHA informed the House earlier this month that CNB has been developing social media content and messages highlighting "strong deterrence" and "evidence-based narratives" on Singapore's drug policies.

sections.label: CNB broadcasting drug abuser data
sections.summary: CNB should, where possible, regularly broadcast data on how many drug abusers would be fed the quantum of drugs found on a suspected trafficker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Where possible, CNB should regularly broadcast data of how many drug abusers would be fed with the quantum of drugs found on a suspected drug trafficker.

sections.label: MDA amendments and Prisons Service
sections.summary: Amendments to the MDA in 2019 helped the Prisons Service differentiate reoffending risks, reduce lower-risk offenders' negative influence, and better support drug offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Aided by the amendments to the MDA in 2019, the Prisons Service has been able to further differentiate offenders' risks of reoffending, reduce lower-risk offenders from being negatively influenced by more recalcitrant offenders, and better support drug offenders in a way that is calibrated to their situation.

sections.label: K Shanmugam on ex-offender recidivism
sections.summary: K Shanmugam told CARE Network partners that while the two-year recidivism rate halved in 20 years, nearly one in two ex-offenders returned to prison after five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Minister for Home Affairs K Shanmugam acknowledged this in a speech he made on 28 June 2019 to the partners of the CARE Network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: He observed that whilst the recividism rate over two years went down by half in the last 20 years, nearly one in two ex-offenders returned to prison five years after their release.

sections.label: SCDF EMS calls in 2019
sections.summary: SCDF responded to 191,468 Emergency Medical Services calls in 2019, an average of 520 calls a day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, SCDF responded to 191,468 Emergency Medical Services (EMS) calls in 2019, or an average of 520 calls a day.

sections.label: Non-emergency and false alarm calls
sections.summary: 2019 figures rose 2.1% from 2018, and non-emergency and false alarm calls made up 9.2% of EMS calls, about 52 such calls daily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: The 2019 figures showed a 2.1% increase from 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: We must, therefore, address this and support them in their work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: However, a statistic that I found to be worrying in the Fire, Emergency Medical Services and Enforcement Statistics 2019 is that non-emergency and false alarm calls constitute 9.2% of EMS calls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: Based on the statistics, the SCDF EMS team has to deal with almost 52 such calls every day.

sections.label: Demerit point composition fines
sections.summary: Composition fines for offences attracting at least 12 demerit points were doubled, with heavy vehicle drivers' fines rising from $230 to $500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For offences that attracted at least 12 demerit points which could manifest, for example, in a failure to conform to a red light signal, the composition fine has been doubled from $200 to $400 while heavy vehicle drivers have seen a jump in the same offence from $230 to $500 in so far as the fine amount is concerned.

sections.label: Loan and social media scams
sections.summary: Loan scam victims lost at least $6.8 million in about 1,700 cases from January to November last year, and social media impersonation scam cases rose.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Victims were cheated of at least $6.8 million in about 1,700 reported cases of loan scams between January and November last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: This is more than three times the reported amount for the whole of 2018, where there were about 990 cases and victims were cheated of a total of about $2 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The number of people scammed by impersonators on social media also jumped by more than nine times in the past three years, with most victims being in their 20s to 40s.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The number rose from 2017's 71 to 672 cases in the first 11 months of last year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The amount cheated increased nearly 43 times, from at least $168,000 to about $7.2 million over the same period of time.

sections.label: Terrorist financing and ISIS support
sections.summary: In January a Singaporean man was charged with terrorist financing, and in February a 17-year-old student was detained for supporting ISIS.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In January this year, a Singaporean man was charged with terrorist financing.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Last month, in February, a 17-year-old Singaporean secondary school student was detained for supporting ISIS.

sections.label: Scam cases and losses 2019
sections.summary: Total scam cases rose 53% to 9,500 in 2019 from 6,100 in 2018, with $168 million lost to scammers in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The total number of scam cases went up by 53% to 9,500 cases in 2019, up from 6,100 cases in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: A total of $168 million was lost to scammers last year in 2019.

sections.label: NTU study on drug crime cost
sections.summary: An NTU study commissioned by MHA in 2016 assessed the total cost of drug crime as high as S$1.23 billion in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: A Nanyang Technology University (NTU) study commissioned by MHA in 2016 looked at the quantitative aspects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: They assessed that the total cost of drug crime was as high as S$1.23 billion in 2015, even though our drug abuse rates are much lower than in other countries.

sections.label: New abusers and drug misinformation
sections.summary: The proportion of new abusers in the past year remained high at 41%, and social media spreads misinformation normalising drug use, targeting vulnerable youths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the proportion of new abusers in the past year remained high at 41%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Today, there is social media and mass media spreading misinformation that normalises drug use.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And much of this content is increasingly targeted at vulnerable youths, targeted at our next generation, targeted at our future.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Other than tough drug laws and strict enforcement, can the Minister also tell us how MHA will engage the community to guard against the harms of drug abuse?

sections.label: Gallup Law and Order ranking
sections.summary: Singapore is ranked first in the 2019 Gallup Global Law and Order Report, the sixth year running.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Looking at international rankings, the 2019 Gallup Global Law and Order Report, we are again ranked first and that is the sixth year running that Singapore has been ranked No 1.

sections.label: Penalties for intimate partner offences
sections.summary: Maximum penalties for rape, hurt and wrongful confinement against intimate partners or close relations were doubled.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: To give one example, for offences committed against intimate partners or those in close relationships, we doubled the maximum penalties for rape, hurt, wrongful confinement.

sections.label: Harassment and Protection Order breaches
sections.summary: Punishments were doubled for harassment of intimate partners and repeated breaches of Protection Orders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Where people harass others whom they are in an intimate relationship with, the offender harasses someone who is in an intimate relationship, and there are repeated breaches of Protection Orders, punishments have been doubled.

sections.label: MRHA amendment and religious harmony
sections.summary: The MRHA was never formally invoked, and was amended last October to enable decisive action against threats to religious harmony.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The success of our policies is shown by the fact that we have never had to actually formally invoke the MRHA even once in those years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I must count as one of those who was uncomfortable with the legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But we amended the MRHA last year in October and it will enable us to take effective, decisive action against the threats to religious harmony.

sections.label: Targeting by religious and LGBT groups
sections.summary: Both religious groups targeting non-religious groups and non-religious groups targeting religious groups will be proscribed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Meanwhile, religious groups also felt that they were targeted by LGBT groups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And our approach is, we put in something – whether religious groups target non-religious groups, or whether non-religious groups intend to target religious groups, both will be proscribed.

sections.label: MRHA explanatory statement on LGBTQ
sections.summary: The amended MRHA's Explanatory Statement explicitly used the LGBTQ community as an example of what the provisions cover.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We should all be free to express our individual views but in a responsible manner.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, when we amended the MRHA, we explicitly stated that in the Explanatory Statement and used the LGBTQ community as an example of what would be covered by these provisions.

sections.label: Trust in Home Team surveys
sections.summary: Surveys show 91% of respondents agreed the Home Team fulfils its mission of keeping Singapore safe and secure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We can safely say, year after year, the high level of confidence and trust that Singaporeans have in the Home Team is very clear.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I have referred to the surveys several times in this House – last year's surveys, public perception surveys – 91% of respondents agreed that the Home Team is fulfilling its mission of keeping Singapore safe and secure.

sections.label: Gallup Global Law and Order Index
sections.summary: The Gallup index shows 94% of Singapore residents feel safe walking home alone at night, including women.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If you look at the Global Law and Order Index by Gallup, which I referred to earlier, 94% of residents in Singapore feel safe walking home alone in their neighbourhoods at night, including women.

sections.label: Homefront Crisis Executive Group role
sections.summary: The Ministry chairs the interagency Homefront Crisis Executive Group, which supports the Ministerial task force and ensures coordinated crisis response operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Ministry also chairs the interagency Homefront Crisis Executive Group (HCEG) which supports the Ministerial task force to get the actions executed on the ground and ensure the smooth, coordinated, effective running of the crisis response operations.

sections.label: Police officer to population ratios
sections.summary: Singapore's ratio of Police Officers to population is 0.23%, including full-time National Servicemen, compared with London, Hong Kong and New York City.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If Members look at the ratio of Police Officers to population: London is 0.34%; Hong Kong, 0.39%; New York City, 0.42%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Whereas we are 0.23%, including full-time National Servicemen.

sections.label: Raising Police retirement age
sections.summary: The retirement age for Police Officers and Home Affairs Uniformed Services Scheme officers will rise from 55 to 58 by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Mr Desmond Choo asked if the retirement age for our Police Officers will be raised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We will be increasing the retirement age gradually, not just of Police Officers, but officers under the Home Affairs Uniformed Services Scheme, from 55 currently to 58 by 2030.

sections.label: First Police Force formed
sections.summary: Major-General William Farquhar formed the first Police Force with just 12 officers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Major-General William Farquhar formed the first Police Force with just 12 officers.

sections.label: Police Coast Guard patrol boats
sections.summary: The Police Coast Guard will enhance its capabilities this year by getting new Fifth Generation PT class patrol boats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: This year, to better handle incidents in our coastal waters, the Police Coast Guard (PCG) will be enhancing its capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We will be getting new Fifth Generation PT class patrol boats.

sections.label: Singapore and Hong Kong police forces
sections.summary: The Singapore and Hong Kong Police Forces were highly regarded, but since protests started Hong Kong police faced violent protest tactics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Singapore Police Force and the Hong Kong Police Force, they were probably two very highly regarded forces in Asia – disciplined, professional, well-respected by local residents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But since the protests started, the police have been caught between the need to uphold public order and protestors who resorted to increasingly violent tactics just to attack the police and instigate them.

sections.label: Public assembly permits and Speakers' Corner
sections.summary: Organising or participating in a public assembly in Singapore without a Police permit is an offence, while Speakers' Corner needs no permit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Even when they were off-duty, they have had to fend off protestors targeting their family and loved ones.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I think one key lesson is that the actions of a disaffected few should not be allowed to threaten the rights of the majority to live in a stable, peaceful society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: And, really, there has to be a zero-tolerance approach to illegal demonstrations and protests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, it is an offence to organise or participate in a public assembly in Singapore without a Police permit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Where Singaporeans want to protest or demonstrate about issues that concern them, there is the Speakers’ Corner and no permit is needed.

sections.label: Danish law enforcement holding facility
sections.summary: Danish law enforcement constructed a holding facility with 36 steel cages that could hold more than 350 persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, the Danish law enforcement constructed a holding facility.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: They set up 36 steel cages that could hold more than 350 persons.

sections.label: Allowing protests in specific places
sections.summary: It is far better to allow protests in specific places and no protests elsewhere, to strike a balance between competing interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: This sets up the police for failure and sets up the police to be the fall guys.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is far better to, say, protests in specific places allowed; otherwise, no protests in other places, because you want to strike a balance between competing interests.

sections.label: Strict approach on protest locations
sections.summary: The approach taken was correct in being strict about where you can protest, not putting the Police Force in an impossible position.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And anywhere else, you do not put my Police Force in an impossible position, where they will have to let as many thousands of people as they want to congregate, and then deal with the violence, as it inevitably, in many places, does result in.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think our approach, the approach we took, was a correct one of being strict about where you can protest.

sections.label: Law and order needs good governance
sections.summary: It states that law and order depends on a socio-economic and political structure that most people see as fair, not on strict policing alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If a large majority of your people feel that it is a fair system, they have opportunities, that the Government and the system are set up to help the largest majority possible, then people will have faith in the system and the people who want to break the laws will be a minority.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But if a significant section of your population believes that the system is fundamentally unfair, the social economic system and the benefits are fundamentally unfair and that it is set up to benefit a few at the expense of the majority, at the expense of the many, then no amount of strict policing and strict laws is going to keep people off the streets.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, the first order or point of importance for any government and for us as a lesson is, really, the socio-economic, political structure.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Then, your police force can go and deal with those who break the law and the rest of the population will say, "Yes, we support it; these people ought not to be breaking the law." So, law and order, yes, but it is not possible without good governance.

sections.label: Road Traffic Act deterrence
sections.summary: It states that the Road Traffic Act was amended last year to increase deterrence against irresponsible driving.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think we can apply these principles, broad as they are, to the specific question.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We amended the Road Traffic Act last year to increase deterrence against irresponsible driving.

sections.label: Fines, discounts and first-time offenders
sections.summary: It states that fines were increased, that demerit point discounts exist for eligible drivers, and that flexibility could be considered for those unable to pay fines.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And I said we got to relook at this.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We, therefore, enhanced the penalties in the Road Traffic Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, to the specific question whether a discount on fines can be given for first-time offenders, we currently give a discount for demerit points to eligible drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Giving a discount on fines for first-time offenders, we might as well have not increased the fines in the first place.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I understand where Mr Pritam Singh is coming from.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And my own approach would be that where people cannot afford to pay the fines, then we should consider flexibility, we should also consider then in giving them some other support to help them pay the fines.

sections.label: HTX Centres of Expertise
sections.summary: It states that HTX will house 14 Centres of Expertise to develop deep-tech capabilities supporting a range of Home Team operations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: HTX will house 14 Centres of Expertise to develop deep-tech capabilities to support a range of Home Team operations.

sections.label: Lab screenings and new facilities
sections.summary: It states the labs conduct about 125,000 screenings yearly, and that a new Changi Airfreight Centre lab and more CBRNE facilities are planned.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: On average, the labs conduct about 125,000 screenings for dangerous materials every year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: By 2023, we will build a new lab at Changi Airfreight Centre and more CBRNE facilities at the future Tuas Mega Port and Changi Airport Terminal 5 are in the pipeline.

sections.label: HTX virus screening kit
sections.summary: It states that HTX designed a kit to rapidly screen and detect the virus after its genome sequence was made public in mid-January.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: HTX stepped up by designing a kit to rapidly screen and detect the virus immediately after its genome sequence was made public in mid-January.

sections.label: Digital evidence search tool
sections.summary: HTX and the Police will implement DIGEST this year to automate forensic processing of voluminous digital data.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: While technology has its benefits, it also provides tools for criminals to commit crimes.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This year, HTX and the Police will implement the DIGital Evidence Search Tool (DIGEST), to automate the forensic processing of voluminous digital data.

sections.label: Contactless immigration clearance
sections.summary: ICA will soon use biometrics technology to let Singaporeans verify identities and clear immigration checkpoints without passports or thumbprints.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Through the use of cutting-edge biometrics technology, ICA will soon allow Singaporeans to verify their identities and breeze through immigration checkpoints without the need to produce their passports or provide their thumbprints.

sections.label: Tuas Checkpoint contactless trial
sections.summary: In 2019, ICA conducted a six-month contactless clearance trial at Tuas Checkpoint for about 22,000 Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In 2019, ICA conducted a six-month trial of this contactless clearance concept at the Tuas Checkpoint for about 22,000 Singaporeans.

sections.label: Growing HTX talent pool
sections.summary: A key priority is growing the talent pool of engineers and scientists, with plans to grow HTX from 1,300 to around 2,000 officers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: A key priority is to grow our talent pool of engineers and scientists.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We have ambitious plans to grow HTX from 1,300 officers today to around 2,000 officers.

sections.label: Officers joining HTX
sections.summary: In 2019 alone, about 170 officers joined HTX.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In 2019 alone, about 170 officers joined HTX.

sections.label: Ops-Tech posts identified
sections.summary: Over 200 Ops-Tech posts with redesigned job scopes will be identified within key Police and Civil Defence departments and frontline units.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As a start, over 200 such Ops-Tech posts, with redesigned job scopes, will be identified within key Police and Civil Defence departments and frontline units.

sections.label: Global adult drug use
sections.summary: The 2019 World Drug Report states one in 18 adults worldwide used drugs at least once in a year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: One in 18 adults in the world used drugs at least once in a year, according to the 2019 World Drug Report.

sections.label: Number rose sevenfold
sections.summary: The number increased sevenfold to 892 within 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Within 10 years, the number has increased sevenfold to 892.

sections.label: Young new drug abusers
sections.summary: Three in five new drug abusers arrested last year were below 30, and one in five thought cannabis abuse should be legal in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Three in five new drug abusers arrested last year were below 30.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: One in five held the view that cannabis abuse should be legal in Singapore.

sections.label: NPS abusers in 2019
sections.summary: In 2019, 414 drug abusers, or 11.7%, took NPS.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Four-hundred and fourteen, or 11.7%, of drug abusers took NPS in 2019.

sections.label: Malay drug addicts decline
sections.summary: Singapore received applause from international drug rehabilitation experts when it was shared that Malay drug addicts fell from around 3,200 in 1993 to 1,800 last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Singapore received thunderous applause from international drug rehabilitation experts when I shared that the number of Malay drug addicts in Singapore went down by almost half, from around 3,200 in 1993 to 1,800 last year.

sections.label: Youth views and NPS
sections.summary: One in five youths think cannabis should be allowed in Singapore, three in five new drug offenders arrested are under 30, and NPS is the third most popular drug and second among new drug offenders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: One in five youths think that cannabis should be allowed in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Three in five new drug offenders arrested are under 30 years old.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: New types of drugs like NPS are the third most popular drug in Singapore and, among new drug offenders, NPS is the second most popular drug.

sections.label: NPS legislation and drug myths
sections.summary: Reviews legislation against new psychoactive substances and counters myths and misinformation about drugs and cannabis.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: First, reviewing legislation to stop the threat of NPS that is becoming increasingly widespread; and second, countering the myths and misinformation about drugs and manage the increasingly open attitude towards cannabis because it is harmful.

sections.label: Inter-Ministry Committee on Scams
sections.summary: Sets up an Inter-Ministry Committee on Scams to execute a comprehensive strategy to combat scams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Given the different domains that online scams can impact, we will be setting up an Inter-Ministry Committee on Scams (IMCS) comprising of MHA, the Ministry of Communications and Information, the Ministry of Trade and Industry and other members to execute a comprehensive strategy to combat scams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: This will include (a) deterring potential perpetrators; (b)	limiting the ability of perpetrators to conduct operations in Singapore; (c)	mitigating the losses incurred by victims; and (d)	ensuring that the public is vigilant and wary of scams.

sections.label: Penalty for false charity representation
sections.summary: A person guilty of falsely representing a registered charity to solicit money faces a fine, imprisonment, or both.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Any person found guilty of falsely representing a registered charity to solicit money is liable to a fine of up to $10,000, three years' imprisonment, or both.

sections.label: In-game asset conversion consideration
sections.summary: MHA considers whether a player can convert in-game assets into real-world ones through the platform.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: MHA takes into consideration whether the player can convert any in-game assets into real-world ones through the platform.

sections.label: LTVP for foreign spouse
sections.summary: A foreign spouse can be granted an LTVP if the sponsor can support the family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: A foreign spouse can be granted a LTVP if the sponsor is able to support the family.

sections.label: SGSecure against terrorist attack
sections.summary: SGSecure was launched in 2016 to sensitise, train and mobilise the community against terrorist attacks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: But of more concern is that it can tear societies apart.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We launched the SGSecure programme in 2016 to sensitise, train and mobilise our community to play a part in preventing and responding to a terrorist attack.

sections.label: AEDs, CPR training, EMS response
sections.summary: Over 5,200 AEDs are installed, over half a million trained in CPR-AED, and the 2017 EMS Tiered Response Framework prioritises life-threatening emergencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: More than 5,200 AEDs have been installed in Singapore since then.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Over half a million people have been trained in CPR-AED skills, of which 75,000 have registered with the myResponder app to assist victims of cardiac arrest prior to the arrival of SCDF.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The EMS Tiered Response Framework was launched in 2017, which allows us to prioritise life-threatening emergencies, to receive faster and enhanced services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Since April 2019, cases assessed by SCDF as non-emergencies will not be conveyed to the hospitals.

sections.label: Civil recourse and criminal prosecution
sections.summary: The first is civil recourse in the Courts for misrepresentation, and the second is criminal prosecution under section 420 of the Penal Code.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: The first is the civil recourse in the Courts for misrepresentation or fraudulent misrepresentation, and the second is criminal prosecution under section 420 of the Penal Code, which is cheating.

sections.label: AGC decisions, trafficking enforcement
sections.summary: AGC decides based on case facts; MHA and MinLaw study streamlining, while SPF and MOM enforce against vice and potential labour trafficking.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: At the end of the day, the AGC has to make that decision depending on the facts of the case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: That said, MHA and the Ministry of Law are studying the current landscape for dealing with such cases, including civil claims, private prosecutions and upstream measures, to see if the current processes can be further streamlined or improved.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On the Member's second question on human trafficking, SPF conducts regular enforcement operations to detect and deter illegal vice activities, and the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) takes enforcement actions against errant employers and employment agencies which may be involved in potential labour trafficking.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: SPF and MOM have a standard operating procedure with the ICA for the referral of potential human trafficking cases detected at the borders to aid SPF's and MOM's follow-up investigations, and they use different methods.

sections.label: Traffic Police instalment plans
sections.summary: The speaker is not aware that the Traffic Police offer instalment plans for fines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The first clarification I have is on instalment payment plans by the Traffic Police.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I am not aware that the Traffic Police offer instalment plans for fines.

sections.label: Clarification on instalments
sections.summary: The speaker says he should have been clearer on the first question about instalments.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the first question on instalments, I should have been clearer.

sections.label: Fine objective and driving behaviour
sections.summary: The primary objective of a fine should be to help people incorporate safe driving and not re-offend, and the Traffic Police will study the suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, the objective of the fine, the primary objective of the fine or penalty, should not be to punish but to try and have people incorporate that into the way they drive, so that they do not even offend in the first place, or if they do often, they do not re-offend.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, I will ask the Traffic Police to study these specific suggestions.

sections.label: Support for ex-offenders
sections.summary: The Member's concerns are correct and work is being done with the Ministry of Social and Family Development to support ex-offenders and prevent youths from joining or rejoining gangs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: Certainly, the Member's concerns are correct, it is something that we are doing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Amrin Amin
sentences.text: We are also working closely with the Ministry of Social and Family Development to see how we can better support ex-offenders, in particular, preventing youths from joining gangs or rejoining gangs.

sections.label: PR application criteria
sections.summary: Each PR application is evaluated holistically on criteria including economic contributions, qualifications, age and family profile to assess ability to contribute and integrate into society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Each PR application is evaluated holistically on a set of criteria which include factors, such as the individual's economic contributions, qualifications, age and family profile to assess the applicant's ability to contribute as well as integrate well into society.

sections.label: Rental housing for families
sections.summary: When there is a Singapore Citizen child or a PR child, the Singapore Citizen and the non-resident spouse can apply for rental housing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On the Member's question on rental housing, I had shared in my reply that when there is a Singapore Citizen child, or a PR child involved, then the Singapore Citizen and the non-resident spouse can apply for rental housing.

sections.label: Withdrawal of amendment
sections.summary: Mr de Souza is asked to withdraw his amendment, thanks are put on record to MHA bodies, and leave is sought to withdraw the amendment.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Mr de Souza, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: We all know the Home Team is a master at multi-tasking, having to deal with COVID-19 now, new and emerging threats and over and above that, keeping law and order in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: So, on behalf of my fellow Parliamentarians, we put on record our thanks and appreciation to all the arms and bodies that report to MHA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: With that, Mr Chairman, I seek leave to withdraw my amendment.
